ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a transition-state structure, and all curved arrows should be ignored. On the left there is a cyano terminus labeled NC connected to the left central carbon; this left central carbon is also connected to a negatively charged oxygen [O-], an Ar aryl group, and the carbon on the right. The right carbon is connected to OH, H, and another Ar aryl group. Reasoning: According to the specified main-chain choice, it is cyano carbon–left central carbon–right hydroxy-substituted carbon. The cyano terminus is encoded as N#C; the left central carbon is C, bearing two branches, [O-] and phenyl c1ccccc1; it then connects to the right carbon C, which bears O/H, i.e. C(O), and bears another phenyl c2ccccc2. Therefore, combining them gives the SMILES: N#CC([O-])(c1ccccc1)C(O)(c2ccccc2).

method.method_draft: First describe the molecular graph in the image, ignoring all curved arrows as instructed. Choose the main chain as cyano carbon–left central carbon–right carbinol carbon. Encode the cyano end as N#C, then the left central carbon as C bearing branches [O-] and phenyl c1ccccc1, and then the right carbon as C bearing OH and another phenyl c2ccccc2. Combine these connectivity pieces into the SMILES N#CC([O-])(c1ccccc1)C(O)(c2ccccc2).
